title: Let Anyone at Your Company Ship Internal Apps with AI — Garrett Galow, WorkOS
talk_summary: WorkOS built a CLI ('wow') plus an internal deploy platform ('Atlas') so any employee, including non-engineers, can scaffold, deploy, and share internal apps with SSO-by-default, secrets handled, and a discoverable catalog. The core insight is that AI made building cheap but shipping (deploy, auth, secrets, hosting, discovery) is still the bottleneck, so they productized the shipping path.

takeaways.technique: One-command scaffold-and-deploy CLI wrapping the whole shipping path
takeaways.what_they_do: A single CLI command checks prerequisites (git, node, GitHub login, Doppler secrets), creates a repo from a template, deploys to a shared host, and registers the app in a catalog — so the user never touches infra.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It basically is a toolkit that helps you set up Git, set up a repo, clone in an example application

takeaways.technique: Secure-by-default platform (SSO, managed secrets, request logging)
takeaways.what_they_do: Every deployed app is automatically behind Okta SSO, secrets live in Doppler (never in repos), and all requests are logged/auditable; token auth is a deliberate opt-in hole for APIs/bots.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of these apps are automatically protected by our Octa SSO account

takeaways.what_they_do: Anyone can push a reusable skill to a central repo; others list and pull skills to standardize workflows across the company.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anyone at the company can if they built a skill that's useful, they can push that skill up and it's shared to everyone

takeaways.technique: Company-wide build days as a feedback forcing function
takeaways.what_they_do: Single-day hackathons pair non-engineers (hands on keyboard) with engineers (consultants) to surface real internal needs and generate feedback on the platform.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually pair non-engineers with engineers. And we actually have the non-engineers do the building
takeaways.numbers: 37% of the 60 maintained apps had no engineer in any commit

takeaways.technique: Invisible infra / single shared hostname + catalog
takeaways.what_they_do: Apps get a predictable hostname under one shared domain and are auto-registered in a catalog, so discovery and access need no per-app sharing logic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we automatically host all of these tools when you push them under workos.tools
